records.text: Jean-Luc Bagur, Frédéric Vaglio, and Daniel Beaulieu organized the attempted hit, and Beaulieu was a retired intelligence officer whom the hitmen said claimed they were acting for the government.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And the businessman who called the hit on this alleged Mossad agent spy was Jean-Luc Bagure. He was the ringleader along with his other free masonic brothers, a guy named Frederick Vaglio and Daniel Bellew. Now, Daniel Bellew was a retired intelligence officer and the hitmen say that Daniel is the one that told them that they were doing this on behalf of the government.

verification.notes: The Guardian/AFP article names Jean-Luc Bagur, Frédéric Vaglio, and Daniel Beaulieu as alleged ringleaders; identifies Beaulieu as a retired DGSI officer; and reports that hit-squad leader Sébastien Leroy believed he had acted for the government.

records.text: Daniel Beaulieu was impaired after an apparent suicide attempt in prison and would be unable to testify about whether he had killed for the French government.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: apparent suicide attempt while he was in prison. And so now he's impaired and he won't be able to testify as to whether or not he was murdering people for the French government.

verification.notes: The Guardian/AFP article says an apparent suicide attempt in custody left Beaulieu disabled with impaired concentration and that it was unclear what evidence prosecutors could obtain from him. It does not establish that he could not testify at all or that he had killed for the French government.
